rules.sentence: Brucellosis (Brucella abortus and Brucella melitensis) is endemic in almost all camel-producing countries, particularly in herds that commingle with other domestic ruminants.
With the development of commercial camel dairies in several countries, this disease should be seriously considered because of its impact on human health.
The role of trypanosomiasis in reproductive loss in camels has been known for decades; severe outbreaks of abortion and premature births have been reported in acutely infected herds.
Early and late fetal loss in these situations can reach 80% in affected animals (A. Anouassi, personal observation).
Trypanosoma infection may also directly affect pituitary function and steroidogenesis (decreased progesterone production or increased cortisol production) leading to abortion.

Prevention of this disease can be effectively accomplished by regular preventive treatment with the pregnancy-safe trypanocide, melarsomine, a melaminophenylarsine compound (Cymelarsan®, Rhone Merieux) during the high-risk season.
Although leptospirosis is relatively rare in nomadic herds of camels, it may become important as more intensive dairy herds develop.
A case of abortion due to Bacillus cereus, an organism suspected to cause hemorrhagic disease, has been described in a 9-year-old dromedary female.
